overlooked_assumption: The agent assumed that the presence of "all-team-models" in a key's model list was sufficient to skip key-level model checks, without verifying that the key actually belonged to a team (i.e., had a non-null team_id).
why_it_breaks: When a teamless key (team_id is None) was created with models=["all-team-models"], both functions would unconditionally skip the key-level model check because the sentinel string was present. This allowed the key to call any model despite having no team, which is an auth bypass. The fix adds `and valid_token.team_id is not None` to both conditions so that only team keys with the sentinel skip the check; teamless keys fall through to `can_key_call_model`, which correctly denies access because the sentinel cannot be resolved to a concrete model.

evidence.quote: However, two call-path functions still unconditionally skip key-level model checks when `all-team-models` is present, without checking whether the key actually belongs to a team:

1. `_enforce_key_and_fallback_model_access` (the main auth entry point for `/chat/completions` etc.) had `elif "all-team-models" in valid_token.models: pass` - skipping the model check entirely regardless of team membership
2. `can_key_call_resolved_model` (used by realtime endpoints and post-resolution checks) set `skip_key_model_check = True` whenever `all-team-models` was present, again without a team_id guard
skip_key_model_check = valid_token.config or (isinstance(valid_token.models, list) and SpecialModelNames.all_team_models.value in valid_token.models)
